_README: THE BENCH (P2, 2026-09-02). Every map Kyle has judged, plus the clean negatives,
as rows a locator can be SCORED against. `preference_verdicts.json` keeps his words;
this file turns them into labels a query can hit or miss.
One row = one map file the label applies to. Fields:
id        stable handle used by scripts/bench.py
map       path relative to the repo (bench.py list checks it exists)
song      song id (data/raw/<song>.zip is the human map; audio in data/eval_songset)
label     GOOD | PREFERRED | DEFECT | CLEAN | UNLABELLED
codes     defect codes the label asserts are IN the map (D1..D6 EMPTY FLOW ELEMENTS)
must_not_flag  properties a locator must NOT fire on in this map (CLEAN rows)
strength  strong = Kyle named THIS file; weak = set-level review, file not singled out
bars      where he pointed, if anywhere. `bars_from` says whose finger it was:
'kyle' or 'agent-read' (the agent located it from the score; Kyle named none)
readable  score.py can open it (perception caches exist for the song)
quote     his words, verbatim, or the reason a negative is a negative
Defect codes (from docs/audit_2026-09-02_buildmap.md and PROGRESS 2026-08-17):
D1 very slow  D2 slightly off beat  D3 drops at the wrong time
D4 not following the main vocals  D5 random bursts of fast non-flowy notes
D6 nps wasted on non-main notes  EMPTY 'feels really empty'
FLOW 'the notes flow in a really odd way'  ELEMENTS no walls/arcs/chains
RULES:
* A weak row can REFUTE a locator (it fires on a CLEAN map, or never fires on a set
every map of which he called D1-D6) but cannot CONFIRM one. Only strong rows do.
* n is tiny. Report counts, never rates. A locator with 3 hits and 0 false fires
is 'not refuted', not 'validated'.
* Human maps are CLEAN by construction of the project's target ('my target is the
best mappers'), not because anyone played them. must_not_flag on them lists the
properties the earlier instruments PROVED humans have (hand-role division,
breathing pacing, on-beat main notes) - a locator firing there is measuring
typicality, not wrongness, which is the audit's central finding.
* `1f333-aplus` and `1f333-before` are THE SAME NOTES at a different offset
(CATALOG A). A locator must give them the same answer.
* Set A rows carry D1-D6 as a SET-LEVEL label: Kyle played BEFORE and AFTER for
the four songset songs and described the set. CROSSOVER and BOTH were never
played and are NOT rows.
* Set B rows are UNREADABLE (corpus songs, no perception caches, FLASH/GOCRYGO
ids unresolved). They are kept so the count is honest, and skipped by --score.
READS live in bench_reads.json (bench.py note). A read that names the labelled
defect FROM THE SCORE, at a bar, is what P2's DoD asks for.

rows.name: Hunger
rows.label: GOOD
rows.quote: The vast majority of the 1f333 song is A+ and better than what we had before so promote it.
rows.note: 'vast majority' - he did not say all of it. Only FLOW is forbidden here: he preferred these notes over Hunger_AGENT for flow. EMPTY/D1/D6 are NOT forbidden - two weeks later he described set A (which contains these same notes as Hunger_BEFORE) as 'very slow ... nps wasted', and the score agrees (64 % doubles, half the human's event rate). A+ was relative to the older builds. tolerance 0.1 (2026-09-02, P3): 'vast majority' = FLOW may cover up to 10 % of bars; q_flow finds jitter at 152-157 (`···D ··D· ···· ··RL | ··LR ··LR ···L ···D` vs human `L··· RLR· LRL· R·L·`), which IS odd flow on 3 % of the map.

rows.name: Fallen Kingdom
rows.label: DEFECT
rows.note: Four instruments failed to explain 'empty' (PROGRESS 2026-08-04). 'Empty' is NOT note coverage - the map answers 69.5 % of onsets vs the human's 48.8 %. Cross-song pair with 1f333-aplus.

rows.name: Hunger
rows.label: DEFECT
rows.quote: Wow, I was expecting the agents song to be much better. The main problem is the notes flow in a really odd way.
rows.note: Same-song A/B, the most valuable kind. Kyle named no bar; bars 33-36 are where the P1 score read found the hand path folding back on itself. Built 2026-08-14 off brief.py density only - predates melody/structure/percussion. 2026-09-02 P3: bars widened 33-36 -> 29-47 after q_flow measured the isolated-odd-16th share on a sliding 2-bar window: 0.33-0.71 at 29-32, <=0.12 at 33-35, 0.31-0.36 at 36-37, 0.43 at 45-47 -- the P1 read looked at 33-36 (hand path folding) but the jitter surrounds it. `worse_than` 1f333-before encodes the actual verdict: AGENT flows worse than BEFORE.

rows.name: Hunger
rows.label: PREFERRED
rows.quote: (BEFORE preferred over AGENT) Wow, I was expecting the agents song to be much better.
rows.note: Same notes as 1f333-aplus at a different offset (CATALOG A, filed 2026-09-02). 'Preferred' is relative to Hunger_AGENT only; the set-A D1-D6 description still applies to it as a member of that set. tolerance 0.1 (2026-09-02, P3): 'vast majority' = FLOW may cover up to 10 % of bars; q_flow finds jitter at 152-157 (`···D ··D· ···· ··RL | ··LR ··LR ···L ···D` vs human `L··· RLR· LRL· R·L·`), which IS odd flow on 3 % of the map.

rows.name: Hunger
rows.label: DEFECT
rows.quote: very slow, slightly off beat, doing drops at the wrong time, not following the main vocals or having random bursts of really fast non flowy notes... the nps is generally wasted on every few non main notes... they aren't hitting that main flow that mappers can generally see.
rows.note: Set-level: he played 'the before and after' for the four songset songs and described the set. Which of AFTER / AFTER_CAPPED he played is not recorded. Codes are the set's, not necessarily every file's.

rows.name: BEcause
rows.label: DEFECT
rows.quote: (set-level: 'the before vs phase' reviewed together with set A)
rows.note: Corpus song, no perception caches - score.py cannot open it. Kept for the count.

rows.name: Kini Naru Ano Ko
rows.label: DEFECT
rows.note: Corpus song, unreadable. FLASH (21e64 or 29a01?) and GOCRYGO (id not found) are the other two set-B songs and are not rows until their ids resolve.

rows.name: Hunger (human)
rows.label: CLEAN
rows.quote: (negative by construction: the human map of a songset song, the target the project is measured against)
rows.note: HANDROLE/BREATHING/ONBEAT_MAIN are the properties the handrole/playfeel/rhythm instruments proved humans have. A locator that fires here is measuring typicality.

rows.name: Fallen Kingdom (human)
rows.label: CLEAN
rows.note: The human answers 48.8 % of onsets and is NOT empty; 1f8d6-empty answers 69.5 % and IS. Any EMPTY locator must separate these two.

rows.name: (cold-cache DoD song)
rows.label: UNLABELLED
rows.quote: (never played by Kyle; the 2026-08-27 DoD test map)
rows.note: Becomes a bench negative only after a clean P2 read; until then a locator firing here is neither a hit nor a false fire.
